address.source: RestaurantGuru JSON-LD (streetAddress '5960 Richard St', postalCode '32246') and cityof.com structured business data both agree on 32246. visitjacksonville.com lists the same street with postal code 32216 instead (single-source discrepancy, not used). This is a food truck: the address is a registered/reference address for directories and Google Business, not a fixed walk-up storefront. Real serving spots rotate daily and are posted on Instagram (recurring pattern: Court Urban Food Park, Hogan St, downtown Jacksonville on Tuesdays/Wednesdays/Fridays; also Apex at Regency Square, James Weldon Johnson Park, and private/catering events).

phone_source: Consistent across RestaurantGuru JSON-LD (telephone +19044054512), Yelp/Yahoo Local mirror, cityof.com, visitjacksonville.com and jaxfoodtrucks.org.
email_source: NOT independently confirmed via a direct primary-source fetch in this pass: Instagram's web_profile_info endpoint returned business_email: null, and the Facebook About page (facebook.com/latinsoulgrille/) could not be fetched (login wall / blocked, both direct curl and WebFetch returned 400/403). The email is repeated consistently across multiple independent web-search synthesis results that cite the Facebook page contact info as the source. Treated as likely-correct but not independently primary-source-verified; phone is the more reliably confirmed contact channel.

website_check.result: latinsoulgrille.com does NOT resolve (DNS lookup fails: 'Name or service not known'). No owned domain found in any directory listing, Instagram bio (bio and external_url are both empty on the IG profile), or search results. Only social profiles (Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, Threads), directory/aggregator pages (RestaurantGuru, Yelp, cityof.com, visitjacksonville.com, jaxfoodtrucks.org, Food Fleet) and a third-party online-ordering subdomain (foodtruck.pub, a StreetFoodFinder-family platform) exist. foodtruck.pub is a platform subdomain, not an owned website, per pipeline rules.

instagram.note: Bio and external_url are empty on the public profile (web_profile_info API). Weekly schedule and location updates are posted as regular feed captions instead (e.g. 'Join us today ... at the Court Urban Food Park 11-2 downtown Jax on Hogan St', 'private lunch', 'Apex on Regency Square 11-1ish').

facebook.note: Page exists and is the source most search engines cite for the email address and for a Facebook-side rating of approximately 4.9-5.0 from roughly 300 reviews; direct fetch blocked by Facebook's login wall in this research pass.

language_source: All reviewed Instagram captions are in English ('Good morning Jacksonville!', 'Thank you for your continued support', schedule announcements). All verbatim reviews found (Yelp via Yahoo Local mirror, Facebook via RestaurantGuru) are in English. Menu item descriptions on the online ordering platform are in English with Spanish-language dish names kept as-is (empanadas, tostones, jibarito). Jacksonville's food-truck customer base skews English-speaking. English set as primary/default language of the site, with a full Spanish toggle.

rating.source: RestaurantGuru (restaurantguru.com/Latin-Soul-Grille-Jacksonville), confirmed via the page's own embedded JSON-LD: aggregateRating ratingValue 4.8, reviewCount 343, bestRating 5. This aggregator explicitly states in its own review summary text that 'Facebook users who have visited this place rate it 4.9', implying its 4.8/343 figure blends Google-adjacent and Facebook signals rather than being a single-platform number.
rating.cross_reference: Yelp: 5.0 / 45 reviews, confirmed independently via local.yahoo.com's mirror of the Yelp listing (business-submitted hours + 5 visible review snippets with star breakdown: 38 five-star, 6 four-star, 1 three-star). Yelp business page itself also shows '124 Photos & 45 Reviews' in search-result titles, consistent with 45. Facebook: approximately 4.9-5.0 from roughly 300-301 reviews per RestaurantGuru's own text and search-engine synthesis ('100% recommend'); not independently re-verified via a direct Facebook fetch (blocked). The task brief's cited 'Google 4.84 / 44 reviews' figure could not be independently reproduced from any directly fetched source in this pass (Google Maps/Search fetch was blocked by a JS/consent challenge); it is close to, and may be a rounding/variant of, the Yelp 5.0/45 figure surfaced by a search engine's synthesis. Given this, 4.8/343 (RestaurantGuru, the source with the largest sample and a verifiable embedded JSON-LD) is used as the headline figure on the site, with the review carousel drawing verbatim quotes from both Yelp (via the Yahoo mirror) and Facebook (via RestaurantGuru).

menu_source: Primary source: the business's own live online-ordering platform (foodtruck.pub/order/menu.aspx?busid=1855, a StreetFoodFinder-family ordering subdomain), fetched directly and confirmed to list 'Latin Soul Grille' with real item names, descriptions and prices (non-round cents/whole-dollar pattern consistent with a real POS-driven price list). Secondary/cross-reference sources: RoamingHunger and Food Fleet feature pages (blocked/JS-challenge on direct fetch, used only for the owner-story quote and a 'sample menu' description naming Boricua Bowl, Latin Soul Bowl and a BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwich, consistent with the ordering-platform prices). The 'El Jibaro' fried-plantain sandwich is documented through multiple real Instagram photos and Facebook video post titles ('El Jibaro Sandwich') but does NOT appear as a distinctly priced line item on the current online ordering menu (only a standard bread 'Smoked Pulled Pork Sandwich' at $12.00 is listed there); its price is therefore shown on the site as 'ask us' rather than inventing a number.

reviews.name: Jennifer M.
reviews.text: Authentic beef empanada that fresh and tasty. And the shredded pork taco is to die for.

reviews.name: TaMisha E.
reviews.text: The best empanadas hands down. My bowlers and I absolutely love this truck. We sell them out every Tuesday but we also found that they are next to the courthouse on Wednesday!

reviews.name: Ebony H.
reviews.text: Love this truck. I tried them for the first time years ago and I've been a fan since day one. They also make a great homemade hot sauce for all the hot sauce lovers.

reviews.name: Jessica Poole
reviews.text: Listen the way this chicken, rice and plantain hit today at lunch. The chicken was seasoned perfectly, and soooo juicy! This was my first time eating from Latin Soul Grille, I will be back!

reviews.name: Brendan Kerr
reviews.text: Some of the best food I've had in a while. The people who own the food truck are very friendly as well.

reviews_note: 3 of the 5 quotes (Jennifer M., TaMisha E., Ebony H.) match the names supplied in the task brief and were independently re-confirmed in this pass via local.yahoo.com's mirror of the Yelp business page (which shows the Yelp star breakdown, review dates and review-text snippets). 2 additional quotes (Jessica Poole, Brendan Kerr) were sourced from a Facebook reviews compilation quoted verbatim inside RestaurantGuru's page content. All 5 are used verbatim; Yahoo's mirror truncates some reviews with '...More' mid-sentence, so only the complete leading sentences of each review were used, never a manufactured ending.

owners.story: Married 26 years, running the food truck together for 7 years. Maritza is Puerto Rican by birth and cooks her family's traditional dishes (empanadas, jibaritos, rice and gandules, and a coconut flan made from her mother's original recipe). Gary is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran (served 1989-1993, including Desert Shield/Desert Storm, stationed in Okinawa, Japan) and runs the smoker and Southern-style BBQ side of the menu.
owners.source: Food Fleet feature page (foodfleet.com/food-fleet-partners/latin-soul-grille) and a First Coast News ('First Coast Foodies') feature article, both surfaced and quoted via web search synthesis; the First Coast News article itself could not be directly fetched (403/Access Denied on both direct curl and a reader-proxy fetch), so these details are corroborated across two independent search-engine summaries of that coverage rather than a single raw page fetch.

brand_vibe: Bright blue food truck wrapped in a tropical beach mural (ocean, palm fronds) with a round logo: a wooden mortar with a flame rising out of it, wordmark 'Latin Soul Grille' and tagline 'The Best of Both!'. Food photography is warm and saturated: golden fried empanadas and tostones, glossy BBQ sauce, yellow rice with pigeon peas, fresh pico de gallo. A dark charcoal/ember base with vivid mango-orange and gold accents (echoing the truck's fire-bowl logo and smoker/grill theme) reads as an authentic BBQ food-truck palette, distinct from the warmer terracotta (La Cocinita Cubana) and bubblegum-pink (Ena's Secret Bake) palettes used on prior Latin-food builds.

images_curation_note: 12 candidate photos were pulled from the Instagram feed (instagram.com/api/v1/users/web_profile_info, most recent 12 posts; several were multi-panel collages the account posts as weekly-schedule graphics with 1-4 real food/truck photos combined into one image). Each candidate was visually inspected. Several collage panels were cropped out with PIL to isolate single, uncluttered food or truck shots; panels containing menu-board text overlays, an unrelated Memorial Day graphic, or an empty parking-lot sliver (a failed crop of a chicken-sandwich panel) were discarded. No selfies or staff portraits were used as gallery tiles. Final set: 1 hero/og:image, 2 about photos (truck exterior + event setup), 8 gallery photos (6 real dishes + 2 desserts), 1 small cropped logo icon used only as the nav/footer avatar and favicon. All images verified with `file` as valid JPEGs, all above 15KB, resized to a max width of 1000px.
video_note: No is_video:true nodes were present among the most recent 12 feed posts fetched (all photos or photo-collages); no videos included in this build. Facebook does host at least 2 short videos titled 'El Jibaro Sandwich' (post titles surfaced via search), but Facebook itself was not directly fetchable in this pass to pull video files.
catering: Confirmed: they take the truck to private parties, offices and events around Jacksonville (Food Fleet feature page, and repeated Instagram captions mentioning 'private lunch' bookings). Contact by phone or Instagram DM to arrange; no separate catering price sheet was found.
schedule_note: As a mobile food truck, Latin Soul Grille does not keep one fixed storefront's hours. Instagram captions from the past several months show a recurring weekly pattern: Court Urban Food Park (Hogan St, downtown Jacksonville) on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Fridays, plus rotating stops (Apex on Regency Square, James Weldon Johnson Park) and private events. This matches a Yelp review (TaMisha E.) noting the truck 'sell[s] them out every Tuesday' and is 'next to the courthouse on Wednesday.' Third-party directories show conflicting generic 'hours' (RestaurantGuru: 10am-9pm daily; Yelp/Yahoo mirror: 11am-9pm weekdays, 11am-2am Fri/Sat, 12pm-11pm Sun) that likely reflect generic/default listings rather than actual daily hours for a truck that moves; the site therefore points visitors to Instagram for the current day's real location instead of publishing a single fixed-hours block.
